title: Software Engineering Concepts Test
description: A challenging 15-question multiple choice test covering MVC, Spring architecture, testing, REST, APIs, and external service integration.

questions.text: Why is the Service layer important in Spring layered architecture?
options: It ensures controllers directly manipulate the database
It separates business logic from request handling

questions.text: Which scenario best demonstrates a violation of the MVC pattern?
options: A controller updating model data based on user input
A view displaying data from multiple models
A view directly querying the database
A service layer validating business rules

questions.text: Why are derived query methods in Spring Data repositories useful?
options: They eliminate the need for databases
They automatically generate queries from method names
They convert REST APIs into SOAP services

questions.text: What is the primary risk of placing business logic directly inside controllers?
options: Reduced separation of concerns and maintainability
Controllers become unable to process requests

questions.text: Which example best represents an edge case in software testing?
options: Testing a login with valid credentials
Testing a list sorting algorithm with one million items
Testing an age field with the minimum allowed value
Testing an API endpoint during normal usage

questions.text: What is the role of BindingResult in Spring validation?
options: Contains the results of validation checks

questions.text: A flaky test caused by execution order dependency most likely occurs because:
Which testing approach specifically designs tests using knowledge of internal code structure?
Why is exhaustive testing considered impossible?
options: There can be an extremely large or infinite number of input combinations
Unit tests replace all other testing

questions.text: Which REST constraint improves scalability by ensuring requests contain all necessary information?
Which HTTP operation is typically considered idempotent?
What is the main trade-off introduced by REST caching?
options: Higher CPU usage but lower memory usage
Improved performance but potentially stale data
More accurate validation but slower responses

questions.text: Why should external APIs be evaluated for documentation quality and rate limits before integration?
options: To ensure the API can fit system requirements and remain maintainable

questions.text: In the Mastodon integration example, why is a separate service used instead of having controllers communicate directly with Mastodon?
options: To maintain separation of concerns and isolate API communication
Because REST APIs only work in repositories
To prevent models from storing data

questions.text: Which statement best describes HATEOAS in REST architecture?
options: Clients should dynamically discover actions using links in responses
REST APIs must always use XML representations
Every resource must have a separate database
Clients should store session state on the server
